findings.title: Main's blanket ConfigError catch also reclassifies mid-verb failures, after side effects, as exit 2
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:147-151 — the new catch arm (the only control-flow hunk in the change set)
src/CLI/Bump.jl:35-36 — `write(p, new)` then `cfg2 = Config.read(root)`, a ConfigError raised after the pin is already rewritten
src/CLI/Init.jl:565 — `Config.read(root; check = false)` after init writes the config
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:855 — cmd_round's `Config.read()` sits outside its own try, so round verbs are the intended beneficiaries
findings.before:
catch err
        println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": crashed — ", sprint(showerror, err))
        Base.show_backtrace(stderr, catch_backtrace()); println(stderr)
        return 3
findings.after: err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)
findings.why_it_matters: The intended case is right and is a real fix: `gbg round bank <round>` against a hand-edited .gbg/config.toml returned 3 ("crash") before and returns 2 ("cannot evaluate") now, which is what the CLI's own contract at Main.jl:109 and :122 promises. But the arm keys on the exception CLASS, not on the config-read call site, so it also catches a ConfigError thrown deep inside a verb that has already changed the tree. The concrete previously-working input: `gbg bump 1.0.1` rewrites the `[tool] version` line of .gbg/config.toml (Bump.jl:35) and immediately re-reads it (Bump.jl:36); when that re-read throws — a config the tool itself just produced and cannot validate — the run previously printed `crashed —` with a backtrace and exit 3, the correct signal that this is a tool defect with a half-applied bump on disk. It now prints a single `config error:` line and exit 2, the same output a user gets for standing in a non-consumer directory, and the backtrace that would localise the defect is suppressed. The same shape applies to any future verb that writes the config and re-reads it. Exit codes are this package's contract and a log is never grepped for a verdict, so an operator or a skill gate cannot tell "your config is bad" from "the tool corrupted your config" any more.
findings.description: The defect the comment names is that ConfigError from the initial config read escaped as exit 3 in every verb but three. A defect-sized fix catches it where the config is read (or wraps the read), leaving genuine mid-verb ConfigErrors as crashes with their backtrace. The edit instead catches the class for the whole verb table, so it changes the exit code and suppresses the backtrace for failures that are NOT "the user handed me a bad config" — specifically the ones where the tool wrote the config itself moments earlier. Both the behaviour (3 → 2) and the diagnostics (backtrace → one line) change for input that was valid before. The fix's own comment claims only the read case ("reported a hand-edited config.toml as exit 3"), so the widening is undeclared.
findings.evidence: diff src/CLI/Main.jl: `+        # A structurally bad config is the documented exit 2 — "cannot evaluate" — and not a crash: an` / `+        err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)`, placed above the retained `println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": crashed — ", ...)` / `return 3`. Base Main.jl (git show af1adec) has the crash arm alone. Bump.jl:35-36 in the tree: `write(p, new)` / `cfg2 = Config.read(root)` — Config.read throws ConfigError at Config.jl:288 ("config does not parse"), :292 ("is invalid") and :297 ("names paths that do not resolve").

findings.title: The prose-shape ratchet's ceilings were raised in the same commit as the prose they measure
locations: src/Scans/prose_shape.jl — the ratchet that reads it (`u.words > w || u.longest > l` ⇒ Hit)
findings.before: "ARCHITECTURE.md § §7.3 The doctor check table (stable ids; exit 1 on any FAIL,",1979,1842,0
findings.after: "ARCHITECTURE.md § §7.3 The doctor check table (stable ids; exit 1 on any FAIL,",2044,1907,0
findings.why_it_matters: SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE's only hold on an already-baselined page unit is the ratchet: `u.words > w` fires the Hit "GREW: … rewrite, do not append". Every unit this diff grew has its baseline row raised in the same commit, so the scan that exists to report the growth reports nothing, and the new ceiling is now the floor for the next edit — §7.3 may take another 65 words and §8 another 94 before anything fires. Nothing here is illegitimate: the rule's own escape is a deliberate `gbg scan docs --rebaseline prose-shape`, the caps that bind unconditionally (120-word paragraph, 3 admonitions) are respected by every docstring row added or raised (the new `pinned_and_managed` at 110 and `torn_check` at 74 are both under the cap), and I checked all sixteen raised rows against the hunks in this diff — each maps to an edit made here, so no unrelated growth was laundered in. The exposure is structural rather than realised: `write_prose_shape_baseline` regenerates the whole CSV from the current tree in one write, so a re-baseline taken for one intended growth silently absorbs every other unit that happens to have grown, and the diff of the CSV is the only place that would ever show it.
findings.description: A frozen baseline re-baselined in the commit whose prose it measures is the self-certifying shape, and it is worth the owner seeing even though this instance checks out. The re-baseline is sanctioned by the rule and by the scan's own hit message, the unconditional caps still bind, and every raised row here corresponds to an edit in this change set. What the mechanism does not give is any guarantee of that last property: the writer is wholesale, so the reviewer's only defence is reading the CSV diff row by row against the prose diff, as I did. A `--rebaseline` that printed the rows it was about to raise, or refused rows whose unit is untouched by the working diff, would make the guarantee mechanical instead of manual.
findings.evidence: src/Scans/prose_shape.jl: `(u.words > w || u.longest > l || u.admonitions > a) && push!(hits, Hit(file, 0, "$k GREW: words $w→$(u.words) … re-baseline deliberately if the growth is new content"))`, with the CSV "written only by `gbg init` and `gbg scan docs --rebaseline prose-shape`". diff docs/prose_shape.csv: `-"ARCHITECTURE.md § §8 Self-test and versioning",1521,446,0` / `+"ARCHITECTURE.md § §8 Self-test and versioning",1615,446,0`, alongside `+"Doctor.jl :: pinned_and_managed(ctx) -> Vector{String}",113,110,0` for the docstring this diff adds.
